Premise holds in code. `find_signal_implementation_run` (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504-509) delegates to `find_task_run` and adds only `team_id`, `signal_report_id` and `internal` checks; it does not check that the selected run recorded this PR or is still live.

`find_task_run` (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:66-77): the plain branch leg filters only `branch=`, `task__repository__iexact=`, `state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True` and takes `.first()` under `TaskRun.Meta.ordering = ["-created_at"]` (products/tasks/backend/models.py:1144). It has no terminal-status exclusion and no `output.pr_url` exclusion. The adjacent wizard leg (webhooks.py:80-92) does `.exclude(status__in=_TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES)` with the comment "terminal runs are excluded so a reopened branch can't fire events on a dead run" - the same hazard is left open on the plain leg.

The pr_url backstop never self-heals a second PR: `_record_run_pr_url` -> `_record_run_output_field` (webhooks.py:275-285) returns early when `output.pr_url` is already set, so a later PR from the same head branch keeps resolving via the branch leg every time.

`TaskRun.branch` is base-or-head: products/review_hog/DECISIONS.md:2572-2581 records that auto_start passes the base branch and `agent-server.ts::syncCloudBranchMetadata` overwrites the `TaskRun.branch` field with the pushed head. So a stale run's column can equal a reused head branch or the base branch ("main"). A bot-authored, repo-native PR whose head ref equals it (e.g. a github-actions[bot] back-merge from main, or a re-opened PR from the same head) passes the caller's pre-checks at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-178 and, once `find_signal_implementation_run` returns the stale run, receives `provenance={"trigger":"webhook",...}` (tasks.py:206-215), which is the privileged self-driving carve-out.

Test gap (angle 2): facade tests at products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1272-1281 assert the branch leg matches a run WITHOUT a pr_url; the parameterized rejections at 1283-1315 cover only internal / no report / other team / fork. No test asserts that a terminal run or a run whose `output.pr_url` is a different PR is rejected on the branch leg. `test_falls_back_to_branch_when_pr_url_not_found` (941-952) uses an IN_PROGRESS run with empty output. Stamphog carve-out tests mock `find_signal_implementation_run` (`_FIND_RUN`, test_tasks.py:32), so they never exercise the lookup.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) "The branch leg cannot match self-driving runs because TaskRun.branch is the checkout base" - false; DECISIONS.md:2572-2581 documents the agent server overwriting the field with the pushed head, and a base-branch value ("main") is itself a collision surface for bot PRs from main. (2) "The initial review path is the one that matters and it does not use this lookup" - true, `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1110-1180) takes `task_run_id` from the receiver; but the webhook carve-out for synchronize/reopen/retarget (tasks.py:191-215) does use it and grants the same bypass. (3) "Auto-started implementation tasks are internal=True (products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:261, master commit 0da0b8dcb7f) so the facade returns None" - this removes the auto-start population but not manually created signal-report tasks via `create_task` (api.py:3795-3804, `internal` defaults False), which are exactly the shape the facade accepts. (4) Guards that do exist - bot author, repo-native head, synced+enabled config, team scope, opted-in reviewer - narrow the trigger to a bot PR in the same repo on a colliding branch, but none of them checks that the run produced this PR. The defect is reachable but requires an unusual bot PR, hence should_fix rather than must_fix.

votes.evidence:
Trigger path: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191-197 calls find_signal_implementation_run(team_id, repository, pr_url=html_url, head_branch=head.ref) only for bot-authored, repo-native PRs; products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504-509 delegates to webhooks.find_task_run and then rejects runs from another team, tasks without signal_report_id, and internal tasks. The branch leg (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:68-75) is `TaskRun.objects.filter(branch=<PR head ref>, task__repository__iexact=repo, state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True)`.

Reachability in production hinges on what TaskRun.branch holds. It is the sandbox checkout (base) branch, not the branch the agent pushes: help_text "Git branch to checkout in the sandbox" (products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:1690-1695), fed as `_branch=task_run.branch` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/get_task_processing_context.py:835) into `git checkout -B <branch> FETCH_HEAD` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/provision_sandbox.py:677-678). A self-driving PR's head ref is the agent-generated posthog-code/* branch (start_agent_server.py:70), which is never written to TaskRun.branch (the only head-branch storage is state.wizard_head_branch, wizard-only, and the branch leg excludes those rows).

The two production creators of a signals-implementation run: (1) auto-start, products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:253 `branch=base_branch` and :261 `internal=True` - rejected by api.py:508-509 on either leg; (2) the inbox kickoff, frontend/src/scenes/inbox/inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:80-95, which creates the task with no `branch` and starts the run with no `branch` (run serializer default None, serializers.py:1690-1696), so TaskRun.branch is NULL and `branch = '<head ref>'` can never match it. So for every self-driving PR in prod, only the exact `output__pr_url` leg (webhooks.py:36-56) can positively identify the run; the branch fallback is inert for this shape. The initial review is not affected at all: it is triggered from the run's own output.pr_url (tasks.py:1110-1128).
votes.refutation: The finding assumes TaskRun.branch is the PR head branch and that branches get reused across bot PRs. In the code it is the checkout/base branch (or NULL for inbox-kicked-off runs), so a bot PR whose head ref equals a signals run's `branch` column does not occur in the production flows; the auto-start run is additionally `internal=True` and is dropped by the facade before any binding. The only way to reach the branch leg with a signal-report task is a user deliberately creating a signal_report-linked task/run through the API with `branch` set to that exact bot PR head ref in the same repo - and that run is then working on that PR's branch (same workstream, same team, still gated by the acting reviewer's inbox toggle at tasks.py:203-209), not an "unrelated PR". No reachable trigger for the claimed approval-of-a-foreign-PR outcome; the team scope, bot-author, fork-safety and toggle gates all remain in force.
